_meta.description: Pre-baked Bluetooth Core Specification snippets shipped with LogScope so decoded fields can surface their canonical spec definitions as tooltips without needing a runtime MCP or network call.
_meta.source: Bluetooth Core Specification v6.3 (via bluetooth-spec MCP v2 retrieval, 2026-05-19)
_meta.regenerate_note: To regenerate, query the bluetooth-spec MCP (search_bluetooth_specs_v2 / lookup_concept_v2) for each code and copy the canonical name + description from the response.

0x01.name: Invalid Handle
0x01.description: The attribute handle given was not valid on this server.

0x05.name: Insufficient Authentication
0x05.description: The attribute requires authentication before it can be read or written.

0x06.name: Request Not Supported
0x06.description: ATT Server does not support the request received from the client.

0x07.name: Invalid Offset
0x07.description: Offset specified was past the end of the attribute.

0x08.name: Insufficient Authorization
0x08.description: The attribute requires authorization before it can be read or written.

0x09.name: Prepare Queue Full
0x09.description: Too many prepare writes have been queued.

0x0a.name: Attribute Not Found
0x0a.description: No attribute found within the given attribute handle range.

0x0b.name: Attribute Not Long
0x0b.description: The attribute cannot be read using the ATT_READ_BLOB_REQ PDU.

0x0c.name: Encryption Key Size Too Short
0x0c.description: The Encryption Key Size used for encrypting this link is too short.

0x0d.name: Invalid Attribute Value Length
0x0d.description: The attribute value length is invalid for the operation.

0x0e.name: Unlikely Error
0x0e.description: The attribute request that was requested has encountered an error that was unlikely, and therefore could not be completed as requested.

0x0f.name: Insufficient Encryption
0x0f.description: The attribute requires encryption before it can be read or written.

0x10.name: Unsupported Group Type
0x10.description: The attribute type is not a supported grouping attribute as defined by a higher layer specification.

0x11.name: Insufficient Resources
0x11.description: Insufficient Resources to complete the request.

0x12.name: Database Out Of Sync
0x12.description: The server requests the client to rediscover the database.

0x13.name: Value Not Allowed
0x13.description: The attribute parameter value was not allowed.

0x01.name: Error Response
0x01.description: Sent by the server when a request cannot be performed, carrying the request opcode, the attribute handle, and an error code.

0x02.name: Exchange MTU Request
0x02.description: Sent by the client to inform the server of the client's maximum receive MTU size and to request the server's maximum receive MTU.

0x03.name: Exchange MTU Response
0x03.description: Sent in reply to a received ATT_EXCHANGE_MTU_REQ PDU, carrying the server's maximum receive MTU. ATT_MTU is set to the minimum of the two values.

0x0a.name: Read Request
0x0a.description: Sent by the client to request the server to read the value of an attribute identified by its handle.

0x0b.name: Read Response
0x0b.description: Sent in reply to a received ATT_READ_REQ, carrying the value of the attribute.

0x12.name: Write Request
0x12.description: Sent by the client to request the server to write the value of an attribute, expecting an acknowledged response.

0x52.name: Write Command
0x52.description: Sent by the client to write the value of an attribute without expecting a response from the server.

0x1b.name: Handle Value Notification
0x1b.description: Sent by the server to notify the client that the value of a characteristic has changed, without expecting acknowledgement.

0x04.name: Find Information Request
0x04.description: Sent by the client to obtain the mapping of attribute handles to their attribute types within a given handle range. Used during attribute discovery.

0x05.name: Find Information Response
0x05.description: Sent in reply to a received ATT_FIND_INFORMATION_REQ PDU, carrying a format byte and a list of handle-to-UUID mappings.

0x06.name: Find By Type Value Request
0x06.description: Sent by the client to find the attribute handle(s) of attributes whose type and value match the given criteria.

0x07.name: Find By Type Value Response
0x07.description: Sent in reply to a received ATT_FIND_BY_TYPE_VALUE_REQ PDU, carrying a list of handle ranges that contain matching attributes.

0x08.name: Read By Type Request
0x08.description: Sent by the client to read attribute values within a handle range whose attribute type matches the specified UUID. Used during characteristic discovery.

0x09.name: Read By Type Response
0x09.description: Sent in reply to a received ATT_READ_BY_TYPE_REQ PDU, carrying a length byte and a list of attribute handle-value pairs.

0x10.name: Read By Group Type Request
0x10.description: Sent by the client to read attribute values of grouping attributes within a handle range. Used during primary service discovery.

0x11.name: Read By Group Type Response
0x11.description: Sent in reply to a received ATT_READ_BY_GROUP_TYPE_REQ PDU, carrying handle ranges and the values of the grouping attributes.

0x13.name: Write Response
0x13.description: Sent by the server in reply to a received ATT_WRITE_REQ PDU to acknowledge that the write completed successfully.

0x1d.name: Handle Value Indication
0x1d.description: Sent by the server to indicate that the value of a characteristic has changed, requesting acknowledgement from the client via ATT_HANDLE_VALUE_CFM.

0x1e.name: Handle Value Confirmation
0x1e.description: Sent by the client in response to a received ATT_HANDLE_VALUE_IND PDU to confirm receipt.

0x01.description: The Controller does not understand the HCI Command packet opcode that the Host sent.

0x02.description: A command was sent from the Host that should identify a connection, but that connection does not exist or does not identify the correct type of connection.

0x03.description: Something in the Controller has failed in a manner that cannot be described with any other error code.

0x04.description: A page timed out because of the Page Timeout configuration parameter.

0x05.description: Pairing or authentication failed due to incorrect results in the pairing or authentication procedure (e.g., incorrect PIN or Link Key).

0x06.description: Pairing failed because of a missing PIN, or authentication failed because of a missing Key.

0x07.description: The Controller has run out of memory to store new parameters.

0x08.description: The link supervision timeout has expired for a given connection.

0x09.description: An attempt to create another connection failed because the Controller is already at its limit of connections.

0x0b.description: An attempt was made to create a connection to a device when there is already a connection to this device.

0x0c.description: The command requested cannot be executed because the Controller is in a state where it cannot process this command at this time.

0x0d.description: A connection was rejected due to limited resources.

0x0e.description: A connection was rejected due to security requirements not being fulfilled.

0x11.description: A feature or parameter value in the HCI command is not supported.

0x12.description: At least one of the HCI command parameters is invalid.

0x13.description: The user on the remote device terminated the connection.

0x14.description: The remote device terminated the connection because of low resources.

0x15.description: The remote device terminated the connection due to power off.

0x16.description: The local device terminated the connection.

0x18.description: Pairing with the remote device is not allowed.

0x1a.description: The remote device does not support the feature associated with the issued command or LMP/LL PDU.

0x1f.description: Used when no other error code specified is appropriate, or to indicate an error code the receiver does not recognize.

0x20.description: A parameter value requested is not supported by the remote device.

0x22.description: An LMP transaction failed to respond within the LMP response timeout, or an LL transaction failed to respond within the LL response timeout.

0x23.description: An LMP transaction or LL procedure has collided with the same transaction or procedure that is already in progress.

0x25.description: The requested encryption mode is not acceptable at this time.

0x28.description: An LMP PDU or LL PDU that includes an instant cannot be performed because the instant when this would have occurred has passed.

0x29.description: Pairing requested a unit key, which is not supported.

0x2f.description: The security requirements of the local device cannot be satisfied.

0x30.description: A parameter value is outside the mandatory range for the specified command.

0x3a.description: The Controller is too busy to perform the operation.

0x3b.description: The remote device's connection parameters are unacceptable.

0x3c.description: Advertising completed without a connection being created during the configured advertising duration.

0x3d.description: The connection was terminated because Message Integrity Check (MIC) failure detected during decryption.

0x3e.description: The LL failed to establish a connection within the configured timeout (LE), or synchronization failed (periodic adv).

0x40.description: The Coarse Clock Adjustment was rejected, but the Controller will try to adjust the clock using clock dragging.

0x41.description: Type0 submap content is not defined.

0x42.description: The advertising set identifier is unknown to the Controller.

0x43.description: The operation has reached the Controller's limit on this resource (e.g., number of advertising sets, max set entries).

0x44.description: A scheduled operation was cancelled by the Host.

0x45.description: The packet being processed is too long for the Controller.

0x46.description: An operation was scheduled too late to be processed in time.

0x47.description: An operation was scheduled too early to be processed.

0x48.description: Insufficient channels are available to use for the requested operation.

0x01.description: Reports the result of an inquiry initiated by HCI_Inquiry. (Classic Bluetooth)

0x02.description: Reports BD_ADDRs of devices responding to an inquiry. (Classic Bluetooth)

0x03.description: Indicates that a new BR/EDR connection has been established. (Classic Bluetooth)

0x04.description: Indicates an incoming connection request from a remote device. (Classic Bluetooth)

0x05.description: Indicates that an existing connection has been terminated, with a reason code.

0x06.description: Indicates that authentication has been completed for the associated connection.

0x07.description: Reports the remote device name request result. (Classic Bluetooth)

0x08.description: Indicates a change in the encryption state of a connection (enabled, disabled, or re-keyed).

0x0b.description: Reports the supported features of a remote device.

0x0c.description: Reports the LMP/LL version information of a remote device.

0x0e.description: Returned for most HCI commands. Carries the command's result, return parameters, and status.

0x0f.description: Returned for commands that take time to complete (Status only, with the final result delivered in a later event).

0x10.description: Indicates a hardware failure inside the Controller.

0x13.description: Reports the number of packets transmitted by the Controller on a connection. Used for host-controller flow control.

0x1a.description: Indicates that the Controller has dropped data because its receive buffer overflowed.

0x30.description: Indicates that the encryption key for the connection has been refreshed.

0x3e.description: Wraps all LE-specific events. The first byte of the parameters is the LE Subevent Code; see §7.7.65.x for each subevent.

0xff.description: Vendor-specific event. Format and meaning are defined by the Controller vendor, not the Core Spec.

0x01.description: Indicates that a new LE connection has been established, with handle, role, peer address, connection interval, peripheral latency, supervision timeout, and central clock accuracy.

0x02.description: Reports advertising packets received during a scan. Includes RSSI and the full advertising data structure.

0x03.description: Indicates the result of a connection-parameter update procedure (new interval, latency, supervision timeout).

0x04.description: Reports the LE features supported by the remote device.

0x05.description: Indicates that the remote peripheral has requested the Long Term Key (LTK) for an encryption procedure. Host must reply with HCI_LE_Long_Term_Key_Request_Reply or _Negative_Reply.

0x06.description: Indicates that the remote device has requested new connection parameters. Host responds with HCI_LE_Remote_Connection_Parameter_Request_Reply.

0x07.description: Indicates that the LE Data Length (max TX/RX octets and time) has changed on the connection.

0x08.description: Reports the local P-256 public key generated in response to HCI_LE_Read_Local_P-256_Public_Key. Used in LE Secure Connections.

0x09.description: Reports the Diffie-Hellman key generated in response to HCI_LE_Generate_DHKey.

0x0a.description: Like LE Connection Complete but also carries the Local and Peer Resolvable Private Addresses (when privacy is in use).

0x0b.description: Reports a directed advertising packet (ADV_DIRECT_IND) seen during scanning.

0x0c.description: Indicates that the LE PHY has been updated on the connection (TX PHY + RX PHY, each 1M/2M/Coded).

0x0d.description: Reports advertising packets received during scanning using the Extended Advertising feature (BT 5+). Carries more fields than the legacy LE Advertising Report.

0x12.description: Indicates the channel selection algorithm in use (#1 or #2) when a new connection is established.

0x19.description: Indicates that a Connected Isochronous Stream (CIS) has been established. (LE Audio / Isochronous Channels)

0x1a.description: Reports an incoming request to establish a Connected Isochronous Stream (CIS). (LE Audio / Isochronous Channels)

0x27.description: Indicates that the LE Subrate factor for the connection has changed.

0x0406.description: Terminates an existing connection. Host supplies the connection handle and a reason code.

0x0c03.description: Resets the Controller and its link layer state machines. All existing connections are terminated.

0x0c01.description: Configures which HCI events the Controller is allowed to generate.

0x0c0d.description: Sets the Bluetooth name of the local device (Classic discovery name).

0x0c33.description: Tells the Controller the size of the Host's ACL and SCO data buffers (host-side flow control).

0x1001.description: Returns the local Controller's HCI/LMP version and manufacturer.

0x1002.description: Returns the list of HCI commands the Controller supports.

0x1003.description: Returns the LMP-level features supported by the Controller. (Classic Bluetooth)

0x1009.description: Returns the Bluetooth Device Address (BD_ADDR) of the local Controller.

0x1401.description: Returns the RSSI for a specific connection. (Classic Bluetooth and LE)

0x2001.description: Configures which LE Meta events the Controller is allowed to generate.

0x2002.description: Returns the size and number of ACL data packets the Controller can buffer for LE transmission.

0x2003.description: Returns the LE-specific features supported by the Controller.

0x2005.description: Sets the LE Random Device Address used for advertising and scanning.

0x2006.description: Configures legacy LE advertising parameters: interval, type (ADV_IND, ADV_DIRECT_IND, etc.), own address type, peer address, and channel map.

0x2007.description: Returns the TX power level used on advertising channels.

0x2008.description: Sets the data (up to 31 bytes for legacy adv) included in advertising packets.

0x2009.description: Sets the data (up to 31 bytes) included in scan response packets.

0x200a.description: Starts or stops legacy LE advertising.

0x200b.description: Configures legacy LE scan parameters: scan type (passive/active), interval, window, address type, and filter policy.

0x200c.description: Starts or stops legacy LE scanning. Configures whether to filter duplicate advertising reports.

0x200d.description: Initiates an LE connection to a peer device using legacy parameters.

0x200e.description: Cancels a pending LE Create Connection request.

0x2013.description: Requests a connection-parameter update on an existing LE connection (interval, latency, supervision timeout).

0x2017.description: Encrypts a plaintext block with a key using AES-128-ECB on the Controller.

0x2018.description: Returns 8 random bytes generated by the Controller.

0x2019.description: Starts encryption on an LE connection using the supplied LTK, EDIV, and Rand.

0x201a.description: Replies to HCI_LE_Long_Term_Key_Request with the requested LTK.

0x201b.description: Replies to HCI_LE_Long_Term_Key_Request indicating that no LTK is available for this peer.

0x2030.description: Returns the current TX and RX PHY on the connection (1M, 2M, or Coded).

0x2031.description: Sets the default PHY preferences (TX and RX) for future connections.

0x2032.description: Requests a PHY change on an existing LE connection (TX PHY and RX PHY: 1M/2M/Coded).

0x2036.description: Configures Extended LE advertising parameters (BT 5+): advertising sets, primary/secondary PHY, secondary max skip, SID, scan request notifications.

0x2037.description: Sets the advertising data for an Extended LE advertising set. Supports fragmented data up to 1650 bytes.

0x2038.description: Sets the scan response data for an Extended LE advertising set.

0x2039.description: Starts or stops Extended LE advertising sets.

0x2041.description: Configures Extended LE scan parameters across primary advertising PHYs (1M, Coded).

0x2042.description: Starts or stops Extended LE scanning with optional filter policy and duration.

0x2043.description: Initiates an LE connection using Extended Advertising parameters (BT 5+).

0x204e.description: Suggests the Controller's preferred LL Data PDU max octets and max TX time for new connections.
